A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SCARLet study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream-task experiments, retrieval evaluations, ablations, attribution comparisons, and case studies, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Contriever and SCARLet-Contriever results on BRIGHT in Table 4.

M1.justification: Shared-context synthesis, entity expansion, filtering and noise generation, perturbation-based attribution, clustering, and retriever training remain unchanged. Figure 1's added enhancement annotation depicts a step already documented in v1's Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten downstream datasets, GTI, BRIGHT, X2-Retrieval, and pooled-corpus evaluation. The added BRIGHT rows evaluate another existing retriever on the same three task categories.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Contriever as a comparator for SCARLet-Contriever on BRIGHT; v1 reported only BGE and SCARLet-BGE there. The downstream-task and attribution-comparison baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes the stated training duration from three epochs to one. Other stated settings, including learning rate, perturbation sampling, test sample counts, retrieval depth, and metrics, remain unchanged. This documents a budget revision without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The entity-search and clustering ablations in Figure 4, attribution-form comparison in Table 8, and HotpotQA and WoW case studies are retained. The additional BRIGHT rows extend a benchmark comparison without introducing a new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the same random-seed statement in Appendix A and synthesis metadata from one run in Table 12. Neither adds repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds BRIGHT nDCG@10 scores for Contriever versus SCARLet-Contriever: 10.5 versus 13.3 on StackExchange, 19.6 versus 19.2 on Coding, and 6.9 versus 8.7 on theorem-based retrieval. Existing BGE results and Tables 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, and 13 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of retrieval scoring, synthesis, attribution, and training remains unchanged. Section 3.1 introduces q for the instruction-bearing query and explicitly includes I in generation, clarifying v1's overloaded x notation. No proofs or derivations are added.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central contributions: modeling multi-task utility and passage interactions through shared-context synthesis and attribution, with improved RALM performance. Revised contribution bullets and conclusion wording preserve these claims.

C2.justification: The Limitations section adds a recommendation to integrate different corpus structures to address code-domain regressions and more firmly recommends stronger reasoning-capable synthesizers. The code-domain weakness and poor GPT-4o-mini synthesis were already reported in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a resource-repository link and explicitly lists the four pooled-corpus sources in Table 13. Appendix C revises the epoch count, while Table 5 loses its explicit closed-setup note. Repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xia et al. (2015) and Guo et al. (2019) to the semantic-relevance discussion and removes Worledge et al. (2023) on contributive attribution. It also drops the critique linking earlier noisy-context construction to low recall and high labor costs; the broader positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the introduction, method overview, query notation, and pooling terminology, alongside grammar corrections and revised limitations. A corresponding-author note and acknowledgments are added. Section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 5 are visually revised, and several figures and tables are relocated. Table 4 gains two rows, Table 13's caption expands, and appendix prompt formatting changes. The basic document layout is retained.

improvement.justification: The added BRIGHT rows make the comparison across retrievers more complete, while clearer query notation, corpus documentation, and resource access information improve usability. These are limited gains: most evidence is unchanged, and Appendix C's unexplained three-to-one epoch revision leaves uncertainty about how the retained results were produced.
